questions.question: The Doppler effect is the change in the ________ of the sound detected by a listener when source and listener move relative to the medium.
options: frequency
speed of sound
amplitude
temperature

questions.question: Ahead of a moving siren, the wavefronts are:
options: Spread farther apart, giving a lower detected frequency
Bunched closer together, giving a higher detected frequency
Unchanged, because the speed of sound is constant
Travelling faster than sound

questions.question: As a siren approaches, it also gets louder. The loudness increase is:
options: The main evidence of the Doppler effect
Caused by the bunching of wavefronts
Not the Doppler effect — it is due to decreasing distance and larger amplitude
Proof that the frequency has risen

questions.question: During the entire fly-past, the frequency EMITTED by the siren:
options: Rises, then falls
Falls steadily
Matches whatever the listener hears
Never changes — only the detected frequency changes

questions.question: In fL = (v ± vL)/(v ± vs) × fs, a source moving TOWARD a stationary listener requires:
options: Adding vs in the denominator
Subtracting vs in the denominator, making the fraction larger
Adding vL in the numerator
Subtracting vL in the numerator

questions.question: A siren of 840 Hz approaches a stationary listener at 25 m·s⁻¹ (v = 340 m·s⁻¹). The detected frequency is:
options: 840 Hz

questions.question: The same siren receding at 25 m·s⁻¹ is detected as:
options: 840 Hz
715 Hz

questions.question: The safest way to choose the signs in the Doppler equation is to:
options: Always add in the numerator and subtract in the denominator
Memorise one worked example
Use whichever signs give a round number
Decide first whether the answer must be higher or lower than fs, then pick signs to match

questions.question: A car drives at 15 m·s⁻¹ toward a stationary 600 Hz siren (v = 340 m·s⁻¹). The detected frequency is:
options: 600 Hz
660 Hz

questions.question: A stationary listener hears a 750 Hz train hooter as 800 Hz. Before any algebra, you can conclude the train is:
options: Receding, because the frequency changed
Approaching, because the detected frequency is higher than the source frequency
Stationary
Accelerating

questions.question: For that hooter (v = 340 m·s⁻¹), the train's speed works out to:
options: 50 m·s⁻¹

questions.question: Doppler flow measurement finds narrowed arteries because blood passing through a constriction:
options: Stops moving, giving no reflection
Cools down, changing the wave speed
Absorbs all the ultrasound
Speeds up, increasing the frequency shift of the reflected ultrasound

subtopics.title: Red Shifts and the Expanding Universe

questions.question: A red shift in a galaxy's light means its spectral lines appear at:
options: Lower frequencies than in the laboratory — the galaxy is receding
Higher frequencies than in the laboratory — the galaxy is approaching
Random frequencies
Exactly the laboratory frequencies

questions.question: Astronomers can measure a galaxy's shift because each element's spectral lines form:
options: A continuous rainbow with no structure
A fingerprint pattern that shifts as a whole and stays recognisable
A single line at one frequency
A pattern unique to each galaxy

questions.question: The observation that distant galaxies are nearly all red-shifted, with farther galaxies shifted more, supports the conclusion that:
options: Earth is at the centre of the universe
Galaxies orbit the Milky Way
The universe is expanding — galaxies recede from us and from each other
Light slows down over large distances

questions.question: In the rising-bread picture of expansion, every raisin sees all the others moving away. This shows that:
options: The raisins repel each other
Only the outermost raisins move
The loaf has a fixed centre that all raisins flee
Recession in every direction does not make any observer the centre

subtopics.title: The Siren That Lies to You

questions.question: To the crew riding inside the fire engine, the siren's pitch:
options: Stays constant the whole trip — there is no relative motion between them and the source
Rises as the engine speeds up
Falls as the engine passes pedestrians
Depends on the wind

questions.question: The pitch you hear on the pavement drops at the moment of passing because:
options: The driver switches the siren to a lower note
The crest spacing reaching you changes from bunched to stretched
The speed of sound suddenly decreases
Your ears tire of the high note

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches each observation to its cause?
options: Louder: Doppler. Higher pitch: closeness.
Louder: higher frequency. Higher pitch: larger amplitude.
Louder: decreasing distance. Higher pitch: Doppler bunching of crests.
Both are caused by the Doppler effect.

questions.question: In the taxi picture, the rank's ten-minute schedule stands for the source's:
options: Frequency
Amplitude
Wavelength
Loudness

questions.question: Walking TOWARD the rank, you are passed by taxis:
options: Less often than the schedule
More often than the schedule — a higher personal arrival rate
Exactly on schedule
Not at all

questions.question: The whole rank creeping toward you while dispatching on schedule stands for:
options: A moving listener
A stationary source
A moving source — crests launched successively closer, arriving more often
A change in the speed of sound

questions.question: The taxi picture teaches that motion between source and listener changes:
options: The rate the source produces waves
The wave speed in the medium
The energy of each wave
Only the rate at which the waves REACH the listener

subtopics.title: From the Maternity Ward to the Whole Sky

questions.question: Ultrasound used in medical Doppler machines is sound that is:
options: Above 20 kHz — too high for human hearing
Below 20 Hz — too low for human hearing
Exactly at the limit of hearing
Electromagnetic rather than mechanical

questions.question: A foetal heartbeat is made audible by:
options: Amplifying the heart's own sound waves
Converting the rhythmic Doppler shifts of ultrasound reflected off the moving heart wall
X-ray imaging of the heart
Measuring the mother's pulse

questions.question: The single idea linking the clinic and the night sky is:
options: Sound and light travel at the same speed
All waves get louder when reflected
A wave bounced off or sent by a mover returns shifted, and the shift measures the speed
Frequency and amplitude are the same quantity

questions.question: In the rising-dough picture of the universe, the raisins drift apart because:
options: Each raisin propels itself
The oven pushes them from the centre
They shrink as the loaf bakes
The dough — space itself — stretches between them
